records.title: Employing Microelectrode Arrays and Optogenetics to Interrogate Neural Networks in Neurodegenerative Disease Organoid Models.
records.abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are characterized by progressive neuronal dysfunction or loss and are traditionally mechanistically studied in vivo by applying a variety of non-human model systems. Human stem cell-derived 2D and 3D neuronal cultures and organoids are emerging as valuable complementary systems for in vitro modeling of human disease-relevant processes at molecular, cellular and network-levels as they increasingly offer more detailed, physiologically relevant context. The ability to genetically manipulate and rapidly scale these platforms for high-throughput analysis and drug screening makes them a vital component for advancing new therapeutic interventions. Perhaps the greatest accelerators of these neural stem cell technologies are functional interrogation tools such as microelectrode arrays (MEAs), optical electrophysiology, and optogenetic stimulation, which are transforming how neuronal activity is measured and manipulated in vitro. This review explores how emerging tools for measuring connectivity, excitability, and synaptic dynamics are integrated into high temporal and spatial-resolution studies to connect molecular pathology to systems-level behavior and drive therapeutic discovery in neurodegenerative disease.

records.title: A modular patient-derived organoid-xenograft platform reveals molecular and clinical trajectories of prostate cancer progression.
records.abstract: Patient-derived organoids (PDOs) are becoming increasingly important in prostate cancer (PCa) translational research. However, direct proof-of-concept studies demonstrating their ability to model disease evolution, identify relevant biomarkers, and accurately predict treatment response in PCa patients, remain scarce. Here, we report the establishment of serially transplantable xenografts series derived from two advanced PCa PDO lines, which can be further re-cultured as organoids. Newly generated model series maintain key phenotypic, genomic, and functional characteristics of the original patient tumors, and emulate relevant molecular subtypes of advanced PCa. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis uncovers transcriptomic differences between xenograft and organoid models, as well as signaling pathways which are largely preserved and can be targeted ex vivo. Functional drug profiles correlate with molecular and clinical attributes, as exemplified by response to androgen receptor (AR) pathway inhibitors and glucocorticoid-mediated AR signaling activation. Longitudinal scRNA-seq analysis of perturbed PDOs identifies a rare PROX1+/ALDH1A1+ cell population, which pre-exist in the treatment-naïve setting, is significantly enriched upon androgen deprivation, and can be pharmacologically targeted. Notably, this cell population is similarly enriched in post-treatment samples of the original patient and in a subset of aggressive AR-negative PCa molecular subtypes across several CRPC cohorts, suggesting a potential link with PCa progression. Our study provides proof-of-concept evidence that organoids can mirror PCa patient-specific drug sensitivity profiles and molecular trajectories of disease progression, uncovering plasticity-related molecular programs and actionable biomarkers. Ultimately, our organoid-xenograft model series provide a modular and scalable platform that can readily be used for mechanistic and translational studies.

records.title: Meibomian Gland Development and Maintenance: Mechanisms, Cell States, and Emerging Experimental Models.
records.abstract: Meibomian glands (MGs) are specialized holocrine sebaceous glands that deliver meibum to the tear-film lipid layer. Classical embryology established the dependence of MG morphogenesis on eyelid closure and fusion, while recent studies have begun to distinguish gland formation from postnatal maintenance. This narrative review examines the mechanisms governing MG development, homeostasis, and dysfunction, together with the experimental models used to study them. Developmental studies place fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signaling within eyelid morphogenesis and link Wnt modulation and ectodysplasin A signaling to gland formation. Adult mouse genetics and lineage tracing identify KROX20-Notch1 and Hedgehog signaling as regulators of epithelial maintenance. Histone deacetylases regulate progenitor proliferation, survival, and meibocyte differentiation. ABCA12-dependent ductal desquamation supports meibum outflow, while NAD+-dependent circadian steroidogenesis connects local metabolism to gland aging. Single-cell and spatial analyses reveal epithelial states and changes in the glandular microenvironment. Human and mouse organoids recapitulate selected epithelial and lipid-associated features, and early transplantation studies show short-term engraftment. Sustained secretion after transplantation remains a central question for gland replacement. Defects in gland formation, epithelial renewal, local metabolism, or ductal outflow can compromise meibum delivery and contribute to MGD.

records.title: Co-expression of NKG2A-HLA-E and TIGIT-CD155 immune checkpoints is associated with immune dysfunction and poor survival in gastric cancer.
records.abstract: The clinical significance of the NKG2A-HLA-E and TIGIT-CD155 immune checkpoint pathways in gastric cancer (GC) remains incompletely understood. We investigated their prognostic relevance and therapeutic potential using public datasets, a cohort of 195 patients, flow cytometry, single-cell RNA sequencing, multiplex immunofluorescence, and functional assays, with particular emphasis on cellular co-expression, spatial organization, and functional immune responses. HLA-E and CD155 expression was elevated in later-stage tumors, and concurrent high expression was associated with shorter overall and disease-free survival. Multivariable Cox regression identified the tumor-to-adjacent-normal HLA-E expression ratio as an independent prognostic factor. Flow cytometry linked NKG2A and TIGIT expression to distinct functional states of CD8⁺ T cells and NK cells from primary tumors and malignant ascites. Single-cell analyses revealed NKG2A and TIGIT co-expression in exhausted CD8⁺ T cell and CD56bright NK cell subsets, together with HLA-E and CD155 co-expression in tumor epithelial cells. CellPhoneDB analyses predicted potential ligand-receptor interactions between tumor cells and infiltrating lymphocytes. Multiplex immunofluorescence demonstrated HLA-E and CD155 co-expression in tumor cells and close spatial proximity between HLA-E⁺ tumor cells and NKG2A⁺ lymphocytes. In ex vivo assays, combining NKG2A blockade with TIGIT or PD-1 blockade enhanced lymphocyte anti-tumor responses and organoid killing, with additional benefits over selected monotherapies. HLA-E or CD155 knockdown also enhanced immune cell function without further benefit from corresponding receptor blockade. Together, these findings suggest complementary immunoregulatory pathways associated with immune dysfunction and poor survival in GC, warranting independent prognostic validation and further preclinical evaluation of combination checkpoint blockade.

records.title: Rewiring resistance in solid tumors: CAR-NK strategies for immune evasion and tumor microenvironmental barriers.
records.abstract: Clinical translation of adoptive cellular immunotherapy in solid tumors remains constrained by a hierarchical resistance architecture comprising antigen heterogeneity, extracellular matrix (ECM) mediated transport barriers, immune suppression, and spatial exclusion. Although chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapies have demonstrated durable clinical responses in hematological malignancies, their efficacy in solid tumors remains limited by impaired cellular trafficking, restricted tissue penetration, heterogeneous intratumoral distribution, and profound microenvironmental suppression. Natural killer (NK) cells complement CAR-T therapy through major histocompatibility complex (MHC) independent tumor recognition, improved targeting of antigen-low tumor cells, and dynamic interactions with the tumor microenvironment. Building on these complementary properties, we introduce a Resistance-Solution Mapping Framework (RSMF) that systematically links major resistance barriers with engineering strategies designed to overcome them, while reframing engineered CAR-NK cells as programmable, living drug delivery systems. Unlike conventional reviews that catalogue engineering technologies, this framework evaluates how multi-antigen targeting, cytokine armoring, chemokine receptor engineering, and related approaches can modulate cellular pharmacokinetics, including tumor-directed trafficking, target-site accumulation and functional persistence within complex solid tumor ecosystems. We further critically assess the predictive value and translational limitations of advanced preclinical platforms, including patient-derived organoids and xenograft models, for evaluating immune-cell trafficking, matrix penetration, metabolic fitness, and therapeutic durability. Collectively, this review provides a systems-level roadmap integrating cellular engineering, tumor transport biology, and drug delivery principles to guide the rational development of next-generation CAR-NK therapies for overcoming multifactorial resistance in solid tumors.

records.title: Organ-on-a-chip as a model for chronic wound studies: Recent advances, future perspectives, and challenges.
records.abstract: Chronic wounds remain a global burden, largely because conventional in vitro and animal models fail to replicate the persistent inflammation, impaired angiogenesis, and biofilm formation that drive non-healing pathologies. Organ-on-a-chip (OoC) technology has emerged as a promising complementary platform to address this gap. Its main physiological advantage lies in its ability to recreate dynamic tissue-level cues-such as interstitial flow, mechanical strain, and oxygen gradients-absent in static cultures. By enabling multicellular integration (e.g., vascularized, immune-competent co-cultures), OoC systems can reproduce selected features of chronic ulcers, such as sustained inflammatory signaling and aberrant matrix remodeling, although no current platform recapitulates the full chronic wound phenotype. Crucially, the evidence reviewed here indicates that modular, application-driven OoC designs tend to achieve higher biological fidelity than universal platforms: task-oriented models with spatially organized fibroblasts, keratinocytes, and endothelial cells more closely recapitulate specific features such as impaired angiogenesis and dysregulated inflammatory signaling, whereas generic chips lack wound-specific features. This review critically analyzes such advances, discussing current limitations in cell sourcing and standardization, while highlighting that modular configurations tend to yield higher biological fidelity for therapeutic screening in the studies reviewed. From a regulatory and translational perspective, OoC technology has the potential to complement, and in specific contexts transform, preclinical research. We argue that its bioethical rationale-reducing animal suffering while improving mechanistic insight-supports its adoption as a fit-for-purpose, context-of-use tool: OoC should be regarded as a promising complementary platform, not yet a full replacement for in vivo models, and its use should be justified case by case rather than adopted by default. To accelerate translation, we recommend a tiered testing strategy in which OoC platforms are positioned between conventional 2D/3D screening and targeted in vivo confirmation, alongside a multi-laboratory effort to establish a reference diabetic foot ulcer platform. In conclusion, OoC technology offers application-specific advantages over conventional models, chiefly in microenvironmental control and dynamic readouts, although direct quantitative comparisons remain scarce; this review outlines an actionable roadmap for its regulatory integration in chronic wound therapeutics.

records.title: Virtual Knockout in the Era of Generative AI: From Intracellular Networks to Spatial and Cross-Modal Functional Simulations.
records.abstract: Single-cell perturbation data have enabled computational models that predict intervention-associated cellular responses. This narrative review organizes explicit gene-regulatory-network simulations, latent and compositional response models, graph, optimal-transport, and dynamical approaches, foundation-model representations, and emerging spatial or cross-modal settings through a virtual-knockout lens. We distinguish representation-level ablation from causal genetic intervention and separate held-out regimes for genes, cell types or contexts, perturbation combinations, chemical structures, and doses. We compare representative methods, experimental resources, metrics, and benchmark frameworks and operationally define a prospective holographic virtual cell by its modalities, regulatory and physical constraints, intervention-conditioned outputs with calibrated uncertainty, and prospective validation requirements. The holographic virtual cell and Design-Build-Test-Learn roadmap are presented as future-facing criteria rather than as an achieved clinical capability.

records.title: Engineering of Microbial Cell Factories for Flavonoid Production: from Flavanone Platforms to Tailored Derivatives.
records.abstract: Flavonoids are valuable plant polyphenols used in foods, nutraceuticals, cosmetics, and pharmaceuticals. However, their production is limited by the low abundance of many flavonoids in plants and the structural complexity that complicates chemical synthesis. Microbial cell factories provide a sustainable alternative, yet engineering requirements increase sharply from platform flavanones to oxidized and multiply tailored derivatives. This Review organizes recent advances according to product complexity, covering flavanones, oxidized flavones and flavonols, and methylated, glycosylated, and prenylated flavonoids. We examine the major constraints at each product level, including aromatic precursor and malonyl-CoA supply, enzyme activity and selectivity, redox and oxygen demands, and the regeneration of activated methyl, sugar, and prenyl donors. We further highlight the need to coordinate scaffold formation, oxidation, tailoring reactions, donor regeneration, and host metabolism rather than optimizing individual pathway steps independently. Finally, emerging artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted strategies for enzyme engineering, demand-responsive pathway regulation, automated design-build-test-learn (DBTL) cycles, and virtual-cell modeling are discussed. This product-complexity-oriented framework provides design principles for developing efficient, modular, and programmable microbial platforms for flavonoid biomanufacturing.

records.title: A low-rank decoder bottleneck bounds reliability in foundation-model perturbation prediction.
records.abstract: Foundation-model predictors of perturbation response are evaluated primarily by aggregate accuracy. Using their predictions to prioritize experiments requires assessing each prediction's reliability. We audit the state-transition (ST) decoder used in STATE across three encoders (SE-600M, scGPT, and Tahoe-x1) and four cell lines under CRISPRi. The decoder's first attention layer has a low-rank output. Projecting this output onto 4-32 fixed directions estimated from training activations preserves mean per-perturbation Pearson delta correlation (PDC). This low-rank attention bottleneck bounds the decoder's reliability by distance to training responses: PDC declines as the cosine distance from a perturbation's observed response to its nearest training response increases. We propose predicted-NN-distance, the cosine distance from a predicted response to its nearest training response, as a per-prediction confidence score. The score has a mean absolute Spearman correlation of 0.81 with PDC, close to the 0.88 obtained with the observed response. Thresholds calibrated on this score transfer across encoders and cell lines, and the score remains predictive of PDC for drug perturbations.

records.title: LeakageHunter-SCFM: Evidence-bounded dataset-lineage auditing for single-cell foundation model benchmarks.
records.abstract: To develop and evaluate LeakageHunter-SCFM, an evidence-bounded informatics framework for auditing dataset-lineage evidence and calibrating benchmark-independence claims in single-cell foundation model evaluation. LeakageHunter-SCFM extracts accessions, DOIs, URLs, and repository identifiers from manuscripts and related artifacts. The workflow canonicalizes resources, assigns dataset roles, constructs candidate overlap pairs, and applies claim ceilings before reviewer adjudication. We evaluated it in a curated development corpus, a locked retrospective external evaluation set, and a small prediction-blinded prospective proof-of-concept evaluation. The development workflow reduced 673 raw candidates to 84 filtered resource entries and 53 candidate overlap pairs. Prediction-visible reviewer forms agreed across all 140 retrospective evidence units; their historical labels yielded F1 0.842 across 132 binary-scored units. Independent prediction-blinded relabeling of all 140 units followed by third-assessor adjudication yielded precision 0.727, recall 0.667, specificity 0.910, and F1 0.696 across 136 binary-scored units. The seven-record, prediction-blinded proof of concept achieved recall 1.000 and precision 0.611 across 52 evidence units. All actionable-positive units came from one record. Restricting this analysis to full article bodies retained 50 units from five records and F1 0.759. Evidence-bounded lineage auditing supports biomedical foundation-model benchmark review by separating identifier overlap, actionable review priority, and confirmed exposure. LeakageHunter-SCFM provides a reproducible triage layer for lineage evidence and reserves claims about corpus membership and performance effects for direct supporting evidence.

records.title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
records.abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

records.title: FeDx-SF@βE assembly for AML treatment via GATA1/SLC40A1 pathway-mediated iron homeostasis disorder.
records.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is an aggressive hematologic malignancy characterized by rapid progression, therapeutic resistance, and poor prognosis. Inducing ferroptosis in AML cells represents a promising therapeutic strategy. In this study, transcriptomic analyses first revealed that ferroptosis-associated transcriptional states were closely associated with prognosis and ex vivo drug-response heterogeneity in AML, providing a rationale for ferroptosis-oriented therapeutic design. Based on these findings, and further supported by a transcriptome-based target-scoring strategy, β-elemene (βE), a clinically used natural compound derived from traditional Chinese medicine, was selected as a candidate ferroptosis-related agent. We subsequently developed a nanodelivery system, designated FeDx-SF@βE, based on alcohol-induced silk fibroin (SF) folding to co-deliver ferric dextran (FeDx) and βE. The resulting nanoparticles exhibited a uniform particle size of 182.3 nm, favorable colloidal stability, and sustained drug release behavior. In vitro studies demonstrated efficient cellular uptake of FeDx-SF@βE by AML cells, leading to significantly inhibited cell viability. Pharmacological cell-death inhibitor rescue experiments showed that ferrostatin-1 produced the most pronounced protective effect, indicating that FeDx-SF@βE-induced AML cell death was predominantly ferroptosis-dependent. Mechanistically, βE-containing treatment suppressed the nuclear translocation of the transcription factor GATA1 and downregulated the iron efflux channel SLC40A1. GATA1/SLC40A1 gain- and loss-of-function analyses further demonstrated that activation of this axis attenuated FeDx-SF@βE-induced iron overload and ferroptotic injury, whereas suppression of this axis promoted intracellular iron retention, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and mitochondrial damage. In combination with FeDx-derived iron supply, βE-mediated inhibition of the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-export axis resulted in intracellular iron overload, glutathione depletion, ROS accumulation, extensive lipid peroxidation, and ferroptosis. Bulk transcriptomic and virtual-cell analyses further supported the involvement of the GATA1/SLC40A1 axis in ferroptosis-associated AML states and linked βE-related transcriptional programs to this regulatory mechanism. In a disseminated AML xenograft model, FeDx-SF@βE exhibited enhanced antileukemic efficacy and favorable biosafety. Collectively, this work provides a combined ferroptosis-oriented nanotherapeutic strategy for AML treatment and highlights the GATA1/SLC40A1 iron-homeostasis axis as a functionally relevant mechanism for ferroptosis-targeted nanomedicine design.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-guided open-source CRISPR tools for designer crops.
records.abstract: AI-guided protein design enables rational optimization of clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeat (CRISPR) components. Their open-source platform, PlantOpenCRISPR-1, targets academic and translational use and could offer a more accessible option for researchers facing licensing barriers, highlighting open-source CRISPR's future potential.

records.title: Design of mini-protein binders targeting CD46 to enhance complement-dependent cytotoxicity.
records.abstract: The complement system exhibits a typical dual regulatory role. Aberrant activation of the complement system contributes to the development of autoimmune diseases, whereas excessive suppression of complement facilitates tumor progression. Cancer cells evade complement-mediated killing by overexpressing three key complement regulatory proteins, CD46, CD55, and CD59. Among them, CD46 has attracted substantial research attention owing to its marked overexpression in a range of hematological malignancies and solid tumors. By overexpressing CD46, cancer cells promote the degradation of C3b and C4b, thereby escaping complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). CD46 ectodomain consists of four small complement control protein (CCP) domains, which provide a limited interfacial area for molecular interaction, posing certain challenges for binder design. In this study, we integrated deep learning-based backbone generation, sequence design, and complex structure prediction to design and screen a panel of mini-protein binders targeting the complement-binding domain of CD46. We further optimized the binding affinity of the lead mini-protein binder via the partial diffusion strategy, achieving a final affinity of 287.5 pM. CDC assays showed that the monomeric mini-protein binder and the trimeric affinity-optimized viral ligand Ad35K++ exhibit similar potency for enhancing rituximab (RTX)-mediated CDC effect. Biochemical experiments confirmed that the engineered mini-protein binder exhibits high binding specificity for CD46 and good thermal stability. In conclusion, these newly designed mini-protein binders show promise for further pharmaceutical development and clinical translation.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence-Aided Design of Peptides with Custom Secondary Structure Motifs and Reduced Amino Acid Alphabets.
records.abstract: Proteins are highly diverse functional polymers where the specific sequence of amino acids, selected from a standard genetically encoded alphabet of 20 (C20), determines the structure and ultimately the function of the resulting folded protein. This standard alphabet has been identified to be nonrandomly distributed in physicochemical properties crucial to both structure formation and function, often referred to as coverage theory. While machine learning models have drastically improved protein structure prediction, success of protein design models lags structure prediction, particularly for custom secondary structure motifs and amino acid alphabets. Here, we therefore bridge contemporary biological theory with recent advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) to develop and evaluate a generative AI protein design model, trained on hundreds of thousands of proteins within the RCSB PDB, for custom secondary structure motifs using reduced amino acid alphabets (RAAs). Results indicate an overall success in designing novel proteins with desired secondary structure motifs for a broad range of amino acid alphabets and complexity of designs. Interestingly, for a substantial fraction of designs, ESMFold predicts a fold close to that of the target structure despite training only on physicochemical sequence space and secondary structure information. The development of this model advances research across multiple disciplines, from general scientific AI architecture development to protein design for biotechnology, astrobiology, and early-Earth evolutionary biology.

records.title: Aligning Molecules and Fragments in a Shared Embedding Space for Property-Aware Fragment Selection.
records.abstract: Fragment-based molecular design offers a chemically grounded strategy for exploring drug-like chemical space, yet identifying fragments that are both chemically feasible and relevant to a target property remains challenging. Fragment-level attribution is inherently ambiguous because each molecule contains multiple fragments and the same fragment can occur in molecular contexts with different property values. We introduce Molecule-Fragment Representation Alignment for Generation (M-FRAG), a property-aware framework that aligns molecules and fragments in a shared embedding space. M-FRAG organizes fragments according to their local relationships with parent molecules and their global distribution across molecular properties. Candidate fragments are then prioritized by their distance and distributional proximity to property-relevant molecular regions and used to guide reinforcement-learning-based molecular assembly. Across five docking-based multiobjective optimization tasks, M-FRAG improves the novel hit ratio by up to 58.00% over the strongest locally evaluated primary baseline and achieves the best Novel Top-5% docking scores for all five targets while maintaining strong novelty and chemical validity. These results establish embedding-space-guided fragment selection as an effective and traceable strategy for property-optimized molecular generation.

records.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces.
records.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular model, steering generated molecules toward two large make-on-demand spaces: Enamine REAL and Freedom 4.0. We compare an offline, preference-based strategy (direct preference optimization, DPO) and an online RL strategy (DiffusionNFT) across single-target and multi-target settings. In single-target optimization for KRAS, the fraction of unique purchasable candidates rises from 10.0% to 25.5% for Enamine REAL and from 4.3% to 12.1% for Freedom 4.0, while drug-likeness and docking-based affinity proxies are preserved. In multi-target optimization, DPO achieves consistent improvements across diverse protein targets, including a 23-fold increase for the challenging CDK4 pocket. These results demonstrate that RL alignment can substantially improve the experimental accessibility of SBDD candidates without sacrificing structural or chemical quality.

records.title: Designing rigid protein fiducials to visualize GPCR conformational states.
records.abstract: G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) mediate precise ligand-specific signaling profiles, yet structural visualization of how ligands alter receptor conformational landscapes in the absence of signaling partners or mimetics has proven challenging. Here we show that by combining generative protein design with deep-learning based ensemble prediction we can reliably design fiducial markers to facilitate cryogenic electron microscopy (cryoEM) of GPCRs at arbitrary fusion points, enabling the visualization of previously intractable states. We validate the approach with high-throughput determination of inactive state structures of four pharmaceutically relevant GPCRs, allowing for key details of receptor pharmacology to be resolved in each case. We then engineered an extracellular fiducial marker for the prototypical β2-adrenergic receptor that enabled direct structural characterization of the rearrangement of key intracellular motifs in the absence of G-protein. Comparison with recent co-folding models highlights major gaps in current methods for predicting ligand-induced GPCR conformations. These results present a generalizable framework for accessing traditionally inaccessible structural states of small, dynamic proteins.

records.title: Mitochondrial DNA in cancer: From molecular pathogenesis to clinical translation.
records.abstract: As the only extra-nuclear genetic material, mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) has transcended its traditional boundaries, emerging as a multifunctional regulator in cancer biology. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of the expanding roles of mtDNA in malignancy, spanning from its intracellular functions to its clinical translational potential. MtDNA mutations and copy number alterations drive cancer progression by endowing cancer cells with enhanced proliferative capacity, metastatic fitness, and therapeutic resistance. These effects are primarily mediated through reprogramming oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), fine-tuning reactive oxygen species (ROS) homeostasis, and modulating mitochondrial integrity. As a signaling messenger, mtDNA leaked into the cytoplasm or extracellular space exerts dual functions: it can trigger anti-cancer immune responses by activating multiple signaling pathways, while also promoting cancer progression by mediating immune evasion and microenvironment remodeling within the cancer. The recent elucidation of horizontal mitochondrial transfer (HMT) expands the scope of mtDNA action from intracellular dynamics to intercellular communication, rendering functional mtDNA a transferable vehicle for metabolic reprogramming, immune modulation, and therapy resistance within the tumor microenvironment. In diagnostics, mtDNA abnormalities detected through liquid biopsy and mutation analysis offer promising biomarkers for early cancer detection. Therapeutically, small-molecule inhibitors, nanoparticle-based delivery systems, and G-quadruplex-targeting ligands disrupt mtDNA function through divergent mechanisms, presenting new avenues for clinical intervention. Collectively, these advances underscore mtDNA as a central node in cancer progression and a compelling target for next-generation diagnostics and therapeutics.

records.title: Transcription factor subtype governs response and resistance to DLL3-directed T cell engagement in small cell lung cancer.
records.abstract: Although small cell lung cancer (SCLC) comprises transcription factor (TF)-defined molecular subtypes (ASCL1, NEUROD1, and POU2F3), whether these predict therapeutic response or evolve under therapeutic pressure remains unclear. Tarlatamab, a DLL3 × CD3 bispecific T cell engager, has transformed SCLC therapy, yet responses are heterogeneous and resistance develops in most patients. We inferred tumor gene expression from circulating chromatin in patient plasma and developed an immunocompetent syngeneic mouse model to study tarlatamab response and resistance. Across patients and mice, TF subtypes associated with response or resistance. ASCL1 tumors were enriched for response, consistent with DLL3 being an ASCL1 target gene, while NEUROD1 tumors had inferior responses and POU2F3 tumors were intrinsically resistant. Acquired resistance involved selection for a NEUROD1-high state with downregulation of the ASCL1-linked antigen DLL3 or enrichment of regulatory and exhausted T cell programs. These findings support TF-defined subtypes as clinically relevant frameworks for understanding tarlatamab response and resistance in SCLC.

records.title: Emerging molecular mechanisms of immunotherapy resistance in microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer.
records.abstract: Microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer (MSS CRC) represents the predominant subtype of colorectal cancer and shows limited responsiveness to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) monotherapy. This review summarizes the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying ICI resistance and discusses strategies to enhance immunotherapy sensitivity. Resistance in MSS CRC is mainly shaped by three interrelated barriers. First, low tumor immunogenicity, characterized by low tumor mutational burden, limited neoantigen generation, and impaired antigen presentation, weakens immune recognition. Second, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment enriched with tumor-associated macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, regulatory T cells, and cancer-associated fibroblasts restricts cytotoxic T-cell infiltration and function. Third, aberrant tumor-intrinsic signaling, metabolic and epigenetic alterations, and microbiota-mediated immune modulation further promote immune evasion. To overcome these barriers, combination strategies are being explored, particularly ICIs with anti-angiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), chemotherapy, radiotherapy, dual-checkpoint blockade, and therapies targeting myeloid cells, stromal components, or microbiota. Recent clinical evidence supports the potential of TKI-ICI combinations in selected patients. Future progress will depend on biomarker-guided patient selection integrating molecular subtyping, liquid biopsy, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence to identify responsive MSS CRC subsets and enable precision immunotherapy.

records.title: Au-Pd-rGO nanocomposite-based Impedimetric biosensor integrated with spiral microfluidics for hydrodynamic enrichment and detection of colorectal cancer cells.
records.abstract: The integration of an electrochemical biosensor with a hydrodynamic spiral microfluidic preconcentrator provides a compact platform for cell enrichment, affinity capture, and electrochemical detection of colorectal cancer cells. Here, we present an integrated microfluidic-electrochemical platform combining spiral microfluidic preconcentration strategy with affinity-mediated impedimetric detection of colorectal cancer cells using an Au-Pd-rGO nanocomposite-based biosensor. The sensing interface comprises a screen-printed electrode modified with a bimetallic Au-Pd-rGO nanocomposite, exhibiting a low charge-transfer resistance (Rct ≈ 140 Ω), enhanced electron-transfer kinetics, and a heterogeneous electron-transfer rate constant (k0) of 1.88 × 10-2 cm s-1. Formation of a mixed mPEG-SH/11-MUA layer followed by anti- Epithelial Cell Adhesion Molecule (EpCAM) antibody immobilization increased Rct and decreased ko by approximately 16-fold, confirming formation of the biofunctionalized electrode interface. Affinity capture of HCT116 colorectal cancer cells produced a concentration-dependent increase in Rct over the experimentally evaluated range of 1 × 102-1 × 106 cells mL-1. An analytical limit of detection of approximately 2-3 cells mL-1 was estimated from the calibration statistics. For whole-blood analysis, the spiral microchannel was operated at a total flow rate of 1.0 mL min-1, corresponding to Reynolds and Dean numbers of approximately 48 and 5.7, respectively, enabling hydrodynamic preconcentration of HCT116 cells. Following microfluidic enrichment, the Au-Pd-rGO biosensor generated measurable impedimetric responses for HCT116 cells spiked into diluted healthy-donor whole blood. These results demonstrate an integrated electrochemical-microfluidic strategy in which hydrodynamic enrichment, affinity-mediated cell capture, and impedance-based transduction are coupled within a compact platform, providing a promising basis for future liquid-biopsy and point-of-care cancer detection.

records.title: Pan-cancer ctDNA panel and PET/CT in predicting true disease status after curative-intent treatment of head and neck cancer: a preliminary study.
records.abstract: Early detection of minimal residual disease is essential in managing head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), and positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) has been the standard imaging modality. Liquid biopsy (LB) of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has been introduced as a complementary method to enhance its diagnostic performance. The study aimed to investigate the performance of a pan-cancer ctDNA panel in conjunction with conventional PET/CT in the treatment response assessment. Patient/material and methods: Thirty-four patients with newly diagnosed HNSCC were prospectively enrolled, and 17 patients completed the study protocol. All patients underwent standard [18F]FDG-PET/CT imaging and a single timepoint LB 3 months after completion of definitive oncological treatment. A commercially available pan-cancer assay was utilized for ctDNA detection and tissue genomic analysis. Statistical assessments were performed separately for pathogenic variants of ctDNA detected concordantly in tissue and LB and for all detected pathogenic variants of ctDNA. The combination of ctDNA detection of concordant variants and PET/CT imaging contributed to the highest diagnostic accuracy in predicting true disease status. Sensitivity was highest for the combination of ctDNA detection of all variants and PET/CT imaging. Recurrence-free and overall survival were higher in patients having a negative LB in assessments of concordant variants when compared to those with a positive LB (p < 0.001 for both). A single-timepoint ctDNA detection with pan-cancer assay combined with PET/CT appears as a promising method for predicting true disease status in HNSCC. Our findings are presented as hypothesis generating due to the limited sample size.

records.title: Single-Vesicle Analysis, Spatial Deconvolution and Functional Circuit Mapping in Extracellular Vesicle Biology.
records.abstract: Extracellular vesicles encode a universal language of intercellular communication-the 'ommunicome'-yet clinical translation has been constrained by extreme EV heterogeneity and the inability to trace circulating mRNA to its cellular origin. This review synthesizes three paradigm-shifting innovations that overcome these barriers: (1) the SCOPE platform, a CRISPR-Cas13/hybridization chain reaction system achieving single-molecule sensitivity at single-vesicle resolution; (2) computational spatial deconvolution enabling non-invasive, cell-type-resolved phenotyping of inaccessible tissues from standard biofluid samples and (3) the Functional Communication Circuits (FCC) framework-a network-based paradigm proposing that EV diagnostic power resides in correlated network relationships rather than isolated biomarkers. We critically evaluate SCOPE against competing technologies, establish its unique diagnostic niche and present clinical validation across oncology, neurology and cardiology. The FCC framework resolves the stoichiometric paradox of EV biology by demonstrating that low per-vesicle cargo copy numbers aggregate across the circulating EV pool to generate statistically robust population-level correlation signals. A translational roadmap encompasses pre-analytical standardization (including MISEV guidelines), targeted immunoaffinity enrichment and clinically actionable EV Communication Scores that distil multi-omics complexity into interpretable metrics. Five unresolved challenges, including the L1CAM controversy in neural EV isolation, SCOPE multiplexing limits and the absence of prospective FCC validation cohorts, are identified with concrete experimental solutions. The convergence of single-vesicle analysis, spatial deconvolution and functional circuit modelling is hypothesized to transform liquid biopsy from passive detection into active, systems-level interrogation of human disease.
